summary: Independent read-only census of every reviews/**/*.json bound to the F2b rev13 pin b2ab6acb2bbe, with per-file sha256 and a pre-registered rule set. Live full-schema accepts are exactly worker-052, worker-071 and worker-090 (3). The controller's pass-08 count of 4 is stale: worker-072 moved accept->revise in place at 01:14:54, after the pass-08 scan. The formulation lead's 0 accept / 7 revise is internally consistent on its own 7 files but is a field-key/target subset: the three live accepts bind through reviewed_sha256 only, so an artifact_sha256-keyed census sees 0 accepts (5 revise rows), reproducing the 0-accept reading as a key-selection effect. 18 files bind to the pin; 8/8 controls pass; the accept set agrees with the concurrent, independently written worker-018 census.

findings.check: live full-schema accept set at the pin
findings.detail: Exactly three files carry a full-schema accept bound to b2ab6acb2bbe: reviews/F2b-review-rev13-052.json (worker-052, reviewed_sha256, full flag absent -> controller default full, scope text silent), reviews/F2b-review-rev13-worker-071.json (worker-071, full_explicit, blind=true), reviews/F2b-rev13-full-090.json (worker-090, full_explicit). No fourth file exists at the measurement instant.

findings.check: controller pass-08 count is stale at live bytes
findings.detail: CF-31's declared set {052,071,072,090} measured 3 accept / 1 revise. reviews/F2b-review-worker-072-rev29.json measures verdict=revise with mtime 01:14:54 and file sha256 5db91bb0781d2af0cf651d23b0fac15ca32da8982791dc0e80ad1bc7dc885a8e, i.e. the accept->revise rewrite happened after the pass-08 scan and before the CF-31 record was written; created_at still reads 01:10:13, so the file's own timestamp does not reveal the move. Any gate reason citing '4 accepts' at this hash is unsupported at live bytes.

findings.check: field-key selection effect reproduces the 0-accept count
findings.detail: Same 18 pin-bound files, two key policies: artifact_sha256-keyed -> 0 accepts / 5 revises (worker-017, 018, 053, 066, 075); reviewed_sha256-keyed -> 3 accepts (052, 071, 090) / 11 revise rows. All three live accepts carry reviewed_sha256 and no artifact_sha256 pin, so a census keyed on artifact_sha256 returns zero accepts. That is the measured mechanism of the lead's 0-accept reading; the lead's 7-file set is internally consistent (all 7 live revise) but excludes the three live accepts, so it cannot be used as a coverage count without naming its key policy and file set.

findings.check: review bytes are mutable under fixed names
findings.detail: Three distinct behaviors in one corpus: 072 was rewritten accept->revise in place with created_at preserved; 052 omits counts_as_full_schema_verdict while 071/090 set it true; and no review file carries a self-pin of its own bytes. A count is therefore valid only at a named decision instant with per-file hashes (this review's binding_table.json provides them for the current instant). The durable repair is the one W048 and worker-018 also recommend: gate reasons carry a review-corpus digest and a decision-instant recount.

A concurrent, independently written census (worker-018, reviews/F2b-coverage-census-018.json#bd560b0451e2, report f3e76da13cb3, measured 01:19:00) reaches the identical accept set {052,071,090} and the identical key-policy mechanism (artifact_sha256-keyed 0 accepts; reviewed_sha256-keyed 3). The two instruments share no code and scan the corpus differently (mine remeasures the controller's and the lead's declared sets under M1/M2 and applies a strict latest-per-reviewer full-category rule M3; worker-018 keys on artifact/reviewed fields and reproduces both methods). Agreement on the accept set is therefore independent by construction, though my later addition of control C9 is disclosed above.

Live pin-bound revises in the table, for completeness: 017, 018, 019 (scoped preflight, multi-target), 029 (scoped repair-candidate), 035, 041 (scoped finding adjudication), 053, 066 (x2), 072, 075, 085. The lead-audit's r3 coverage adjudication (reviews/G-FORM-final-verify-r3.json) was being rewritten concurrently during this census (sha256 785373093162... measured at 01:18 and d94dd2d5b778... at 01:21), so it is cited nowhere as evidence. All counts here are void when F2b bytes move (rev14 is authorized, deadline 02:15); re-run census_f2b_017.py at the new pin.
